comment: Lossless is still not true lossless on Windows or Android, and they want another dollar for it? Spotify isn't the bottleneck for sound, Tidal already does this properly. I'm keeping my library here for now because the recommendations are still better, but I can't tell the difference on my earbuds anyway.

Oh great, more money for a service that pays artists nothing and keeps shoving AI slop into my Discover Weekly. I already left over that and moved to Apple Music, so this just confirms I made the right call. Enjoy the extra two bucks, Spotify.

Honestly a dollar more is fine for me. I'm not going to rebuild all my playlists somewhere else, and the search and multi-device sync are still worth it. If they start messing with the playlist tools I'd reconsider, but for now I'm keeping the subscription.
Still worth it for me. Two bucks more a month and I'm still paying way less than buying the albums I listen to. Ads on podcasts are annoying but I've been paying since forever and no complaints here.

Another increase and people still act shocked. This is the best deal in entertainment: nearly every song ever recorded, ad-free and offline, for about 13 bucks a month. Pay the artists, it's massively undervalued. Still worth it for me.

Love-hate relationship as always. Another price bump and Discover Weekly is still recycling the same top 40. I'm not going anywhere though, my playlists and liked songs are here and I need the library for transcription. A dollar here or there I can live with.
Doesn't affect me. I'm on Bluetooth and 320 kbps is fine, nobody can hear the difference. I'd rather they spend the money on library tools than on lossless hype.

Family plan went up two bucks. Annoying, yeah, but split six ways it's still under 4 a person and I'm not going to find that anywhere else. The address rules and lockouts are my real problem, the price is whatever.

Duo went up two bucks. Not thrilled, but Discover Weekly is still my Monday thing so I'll stay. Would be nicer if the new features actually showed up on my account at the same time as the price hike lol.

Premium is a rip-off at twelve bucks, I'm not paying that. Free is ass but I can still listen with ads. If they keep moving stuff behind the paywall I'll just buy YouTube Premium instead of paying Spotify.

Prices going up again and my playlists still play random stuff instead of what I picked. Premium lapsed once and my lists went empty, so is anyone else seeing this? If it doesn't get better I'm looking at Apple Music again, but for now I'll keep paying.

Price goes up and the artists still get pennies while the CEO gets rich. Spotify is a money vacuum. I'd rather buy music directly from artists, I already do when I can. I'll keep the sub to support them a little but this is annoying.

They raise prices while AI tracks flood the catalog and ghost artists get paid? I already left and I'm not coming back until they stop the fake music crap. Pay the artists, Spotify, or stop acting like you care.

Premium goes up and shuffle still plays the same 10-15 songs out of my 9000 track playlist. Great. I'll stay because the big playlists are here and moving them is a nightmare, but I'm not thrilled. Smart shuffle is still broken.

Family plan goes up and I still can't see the full discography on the app? Nope. I was about to cancel over the bad recs on the TV, and this makes it worse. Would leave for SoundCloud if the artist pages stay broken.

Student went up a dollar, still way cheaper than full price so I'm fine with it. My worry is the Hulu bundle going away when the four year discount runs out. Gonna re-verify my student status now before the renewal.

Price goes up again and YouTube Premium already gives me a music player, so Spotify makes less and less sense. Jam is the only reason I stay. If the same recommendations keep repeating I'm moving to YouTube Music.
Price up while the playback bugs are still there? Lol, no. Lossless sounds great when it works but the queue keeps restarting songs. If this doesn't get fixed I'm moving to Apple Music.

Price bump, not thrilled, but I'd still rather keep my playlists and podcasts in one app than split them up. The podcast experience is what I'd pay to see fixed. If New Episodes doesn't come back I'm moving to Pocket Casts.

Worth every penny. Two bucks more is nothing for music, podcasts and audiobooks in one app, and the family plan is still cheap per person. Shuffle is bad and the podcast ads are loud, but I'm not going anywhere.

Did they put the price up on existing subs? Did anyone get an email yet? My main worry is still being charged after I cancel, so I'm checking my billing period before I do anything else. Still have Premium until it ends.

Price up again and I still don't have that setting after years of paying. Ads keep increasing too. The app is convenient enough that I'll keep the subscription for now, but if more features get removed I'm out.

Apple Music is cheaper with better audio and now Spotify goes up? I'm stuck with Spotify for the playlists and the friends, but every price bump makes me want to try Apple Music again for a month. Maybe this is the one.

Paying more for Premium and I still get unskippable Spotify ads in my podcasts? That's double dipping. I'm done listening to podcasts here, I'm moving to Apple Podcasts, and I'll delete my account if I hear one more ad.

Price goes up again and the app still breaks after every update. Amazon Music is cheaper and has playlists Spotify is missing. I keep my playlists here and hope for a fix, but I'm tired of paying for something that won't play the next song.

price going up and the same bug is still here after reinstalling everything. i tried the usual fixes, nothing worked for me. if it's not fixed soon i'm moving to youtube music, not paying more for something that doesn't work lol

Another price rise and lossless and the AI playlists are still region locked here. Same price as everyone else but fewer features, and the discovery stuff keeps getting worse. Still worth its weight in gold for my parents though.

Premium is going up? For a few extras behind the paywall? Ridiculous at this point. I'm sticking with the free plan and I'll listen to full albums on YouTube when I need them. Why do I have to pay for basic features?
